options.radiante.title: Radiante Settings...
CPU threads that build chunk geometry. More loads new areas faster but takes CPU from the game; lower it if the game stutters.
options.radiante.chunk_building_batch_si: Chunk sections sent per build. Higher fills the world faster but can cause frame spikes while loading; lower is smoother.
options.radiante.chunk_building_total_ba: How many builds can run at once. Higher loads faster and uses more video memory; lower it if you get hitches or run out of VRAM.
Light-emitting blocks (torches, lava, glowstone) light up their surroundings. Off is a bit faster, but they only glow themselves.
options.radiante.biome_ambiance_strength: How thick each biome's haze is. Lower for clearer views, higher for more atmosphere. No effect on performance.
options.radiante.cloud_mode.tooltip:
How clouds are drawn.
Volumetric: real 3D clouds with shadows, the slowest.
Vanilla: cheaper.
Off: fastest.
options.radiante.dlss_mode.tooltip:
The resolution DLSS renders at before upscaling.
DLAA: full resolution, sharpest and slowest.
Quality to Ultra Performance: faster and softer at each step.
Custom: set it yourself with Render Resolution.
options.radiante.ray_reconstruction.tool: DLSS's AI denoiser for NVIDIA RTX: sharper reflections and fewer smears than NRD. Off uses NRD, which can help if you see ghosting.
options.radiante.frame_generation.toolti: Generates extra frames with %s for smoother motion on high refresh monitors, at the cost of a little input latency. Not available with HDR output.
render_pipeline.module.ray_tracing.attri: Off
Vanilla

message.radiante.ray_tracing_unavailable: Ray tracing is not available on this system
options.radiante.unavailable.hardware: Radiante needs hardware ray tracing (VK_KHR_ray_tracing_pipeline), which this system does not report.
options.radiante.unavailable.opengl: Radiante needs Vulkan, and the game is on OpenGL. Set Graphics API to Prefer Vulkan or Default and restart.
screen.radiante.unsupported.title: Radiante: ray tracing unavailable
screen.radiante.unsupported.message:
Radiante needs hardware ray tracing (VK_KHR_ray_tracing_pipeline), and this system does not report it.

The game keeps using Minecraft's own renderer.
screen.radiante.opengl.title: Switched to OpenGL
screen.radiante.opengl.message: The game will use OpenGL on the next start. Radiante stays off until you switch back.
screen.radiante.unsupported.message.open:
The game is on OpenGL, and ray tracing needs Vulkan.

Switch to Vulkan and restart to use Radiante.
screen.radiante.unsupported.message.fail:
The last start did not finish, or another Minecraft was opening at the same time, so this session started on OpenGL.

Restart the game, one instance at a time, to use Radiante.
screen.radiante.unsupported.message.init:
The renderer did not start this time. This often happens when several Minecraft instances open at once, or when video memory runs short.

Close the other instances and restart. If it repeats, check logs/latest.log.
screen.radiante.vulkan.title: Switched to Vulkan
screen.radiante.vulkan.message: The game will use Vulkan on the next start. Restart it to use Radiante.
options.radiante.biome_ambiance.tooltip: Gives each biome its own subtle air and water tint, such as warm dust in deserts, green murk in swamps and cold mist over snow. Fades between biomes and works with or without Volumetric Fog.
options.radiante.block_light_sampling.to: Surfaces aim a shadow ray at nearby light blocks (torches, lava, lamps). Much less noise at night and in caves, for a small cost. Needs Block Emission.
options.radiante.sun_path.tooltip:
How the sun and moon cross the sky.
Vanilla: straight overhead.
Tilted: leans 10 degrees south.
Custom: set it under Advanced.
options.radiante.sun_path_tilt.tooltip: How far the sun's path leans from straight overhead. Positive leans south, negative north. Shadows follow it.
options.radiante.sun_path_azimuth.toolti: Turns the sun's path around the sky. Positive turns it clockwise seen from above. Shadows follow it.
options.radiante.sun_sprite_rotation.too: Turns the sun's square around its own centre. Only how it looks; the light is the same.
options.radiante.moon_follows_sun.toolti: The moon follows the sun's path, opposite it, as in vanilla. Off gives the moon its own tilt and rotation.
options.radiante.moon_path_tilt.tooltip: How far the moon's path leans from straight overhead. Positive leans south, negative north.
options.radiante.moon_path_azimuth.toolt: Turns the moon's path around the sky. Positive turns it clockwise seen from above.
options.radiante.moon_sprite_rotation.to: Turns the moon's square around its own centre. Only how it looks; the light is the same.
options.radiante.vanilla_celestial_orien: Keeps the sun and moon squares lined up with their path like vanilla, instead of turning as they cross the sky.
options.radiante.first_person_shadow.too: Draws the player in first person so you cast a shadow and show up in water and glass reflections.
options.radiante.held_item_light.tooltip: A torch, lantern or other light source held in either hand lights up its surroundings.
options.radiante.day_brightness.tooltip: Brightness of sunlight and the daytime sky. 100% is the shader pack's own.
options.radiante.night_brightness.toolti: Brightness of moonlight and the night sky. 100% is the shader pack's own.
options.radiante.quality.tooltip: Sets the most demanding settings at once: DLSS Mode, Block Light Sampling, Volumetric Fog, Clouds and Render Distance. Changing any of them shows Custom.
options.radiante.reset_defaults.tooltip: Puts every Radiante setting back to its default. Hold Ctrl to rebuild the shaders instead.
options.radiante.emission_brightness.too: Brightness of blocks that give off light (torches, lava, glowstone).
options.radiante.held_light_brightness.t: Brightness of held items such as a torch, lantern or lava bucket, both their glow and the light they cast.
options.radiante.block_outline.tooltip: The outline around the block under the crosshair.
options.radiante.parallax_transparent_ed: With parallax resource packs, the carved part at a block's outer edges is see-through. Off shows the border colour instead.
options.radiante.volumetric_fog_strength: How thick the fog showing sunbeams and light shafts is. Lower it if the fog feels too heavy. No effect on performance.
options.radiante.hdr_output.tooltip: Shows the world in HDR on an HDR display, with sunlight, lava and lamps brighter than white. Needs HDR on in Windows and a restart.
options.radiante.hdr_output.tooltip_pend: On, but not running yet: restart the game and check that HDR is on in Windows.
options.radiante.hdr_peak.tooltip: The brightest your display can show, in nits. Highlights are fitted under this.
options.radiante.hdr_paper_white.tooltip: Brightness of menus, text and ordinary surfaces, in nits. Raise it in a bright room, lower it in a dark one.
options.radiante.hdr_debug_view.tooltip: Tints SDR content (menus, text) blue. What keeps its normal colour is the HDR world.
options.radiante.ray_bounces.tooltip: How many times light bounces off surfaces (1-128). Fewer is much faster; above 4 costs a lot, and past 8 the picture barely changes.
options.radiante.parallax.tooltip: Adds depth to resource pack textures with height maps, so bricks and stones stand out. Off is flat and faster.
options.radiante.bedrock_materials.toolt: For Bedrock RTX packs (.mcpack): reads metal, roughness and shine straight from the pack's MER maps, as Bedrock does. No effect on Java packs.
Samples per ray for volumetric fog. Lower is faster and a little noisier; higher is smoother and slower.
options.radiante.atmosphere_style.toolti: Bedrock: sky and sunlight colours of Bedrock RTX, read from a Bedrock install on this PC. Java: Radiante's own sky. Falls back to Java without the Bedrock files.
options.radiante.advanced.tooltip: Shows every pipeline and shader setting below the usual ones. Turning it off only hides them; their values stay in effect.
options.radiante.picture_style.tooltip:
The colour and contrast look.
Natural: physically based light and colour.
Bedrock: like Bedrock RTX, more saturated and brighter.
Vivid: stronger contrast and colour.
options.radiante.tone_method.tooltip:
How bright light is fitted to the screen.
PBR Neutral: keeps colours true.
ACES: filmic, with more contrast.
Reinhard: soft and flat.
options.radiante.tunable.saturation.tool: How colourful the image is. 100% is unchanged.
options.radiante.tunable.exposure_adapta: How far exposure adapts to what you look at. Lower keeps dark rooms dark and daylight bright; 100% always evens the image out.
options.radiante.tunable.exposure_bias.t: Overall brightness of the image, in photographic stops.
options.radiante.tunable.bounce_light.to: How much light carries on after bouncing off surfaces. Higher fills rooms from a single patch of sunlight; 100% is physically based.
options.radiante.tunable.sky_light.toolt: How strongly the open sky lights the world. Higher brightens shade under buildings and trees.
options.radiante.tunable.glass_reflectio: How much of the sky windows show on top of what is behind them. 0% is perfectly clear glass.
options.radiante.tunable.water_texture.t: How much of the resource pack's water texture shows over the surface, as Bedrock RTX draws it. 0% is clear, see-through water without the pattern.
options.radiante.tunable.portal_transpar: How much of the pack's see-through share a Nether portal keeps. 100% is as the resource pack draws it, 0% is an opaque portal.
options.radiante.tunable.rain_opacity.to: How much of each rain streak shows. Low is thin, nearly clear water; 100% is an opaque sheet of the pack's rain texture.
options.radiante.tunable.water_clear_tea: How far the water of every biome is moved towards clear teal water: red is absorbed within a few blocks while green and blue carry on for dozens, so you see the bottom and the light shafts far off. 0% is the pack's own water.
options.radiante.tunable.texture_contras: How deep and contrasted block and entity colours look. 100% matches Bedrock RTX; lower is paler and flatter.
options.radiante.renderer_profile.toolti:
The overall look of the renderer.
Bedrock RTX (Enhanced): that game's sky, sunlight, exposure, glass, water and fog, plus extras such as glowing end portals.
Realistic: less fill light and bounce, natural contrast and colour, little bloom, finer water waves, clearer teal water and slower eye adaptation.
Custom: a profile with settings changed by hand.
options.radiante.tunable.light_shafts.to: Beams of light through windows, skylights and leaves. Needs Volumetric Fog.
options.radiante.tunable.water_waves.too: How rough the water surface is. 0% is a flat, mirror-like surface.
options.radiante.tunable.water_density.t: How quickly the water fades out with distance, from the inside. Lower is clearer.
Shafts of sunlight through the water surface while under water.
options.radiante.apply.tooltip: Apply the changes now and keep the screen open.
options.radiante.undo.tooltip: Discard the changes made since the last Apply.
options.radiante.subtitle: Ray tracing
options.radiante.applying.detail: Compiling shaders. Progress is shown in the window title; this can take a moment.
options.radiante.upscaler_mode.tooltip:
The resolution traced before FSR or XeSS scales it to the screen.
Native AA: every pixel traced, sharpest and slowest.
Lower modes: faster and softer at each step.
Custom: set it yourself with Render Resolution.
options.radiante.restart.hint: Takes effect after restarting the game.
options.radiante.restart.title: Restart required
options.radiante.restart.message: These changes take effect the next time the game starts:
options.radiante.rain_wetness.tooltip: Surfaces under open sky turn darker and glossy while it rains, and dry slowly after it stops.
options.radiante.cache_deep_bounces.tool: After the first bounce, light comes from the radiance cache instead of being traced further, as in Bedrock RTX. Much faster near many lights; bounced light can look softer.
options.radiante.bedrock_one_bounce.tool: Like Bedrock RTX: traces only one bounce and takes the rest from the radiance cache. The biggest speedup; uncached spots may be briefly darker.
options.radiante.transparent_checkerboar: Water and glass trace either reflection or refraction per pixel, in a checkerboard, as in Bedrock RTX. One ray per pixel instead of two.
options.radiante.seamless_glass.tooltip: Hides the frame around each glass block, so a glass wall looks like one sheet.
options.radiante.cloud_shadows.tooltip: Volumetric clouds cast soft shadows on the ground. Needs Clouds set to Volumetric.
options.radiante.frame_generation_backen:
Which frame generation to use.
Auto: DLSS where supported, otherwise FSR.
FSR: works with any upscaler but only doubles the frame rate.
options.radiante.restir.tooltip: Reuses the block lights each pixel picked over time and across neighbouring pixels. Much less noise in rooms with many lights. Needs Block Light Sampling.
options.radiante.ser.tooltip: NVIDIA RTX 40 and newer: groups rays by what they hit, which usually raises frame rate. Experimental: water can look white.
options.radiante.motion_blur.tooltip: Smears moving things along their motion, like a camera. Changing it rebuilds the shaders.
options.radiante.depth_of_field.tooltip: Keeps what you look at sharp and blurs what is much nearer or farther. Changing it rebuilds the shaders.
options.radiante.fog_style.tooltip:
How volumetric fog is made.
Froxel: a cached 3D grid, cheaper, with sharper light shafts and glowing block lights.
Radiante: per-pixel marching, exact but slower.
options.radiante.volumetric_fog.tooltip: Ray marches the air like Bedrock RTX, so sun and moonlight scatter in fog and trees and terrain cast light shafts. Costs noticeably more than plain haze.
options.radiante.reflex.tooltip: Low latency mode: starts each frame as late as possible to cut input lag. NVIDIA GPUs only.
screen.radiante.download.dlss.title: NVIDIA DLSS
screen.radiante.download.dlss.message: DLSS gives better performance and a cleaner image on NVIDIA RTX. Download it from NVIDIA (about %s MB); it is used from the next start. FSR works meanwhile.
screen.radiante.download.xess.title: Intel XeSS
screen.radiante.download.xess.message: Download Intel XeSS upscaling from Intel (about %s MB); it is used from the next start. FSR works meanwhile.
screen.radiante.download.dlss.update: A newer DLSS (%s) is available from NVIDIA (about %s MB). It is used from the next start; your current one works meanwhile.
screen.radiante.download.xess.update: A newer XeSS (%s) is available from Intel (about %s MB). It is used from the next start; your current one works meanwhile.
screen.radiante.download.finished: Done. Restart the game to use it.
screen.radiante.download.delete.message: Remove the downloaded files? You can download them again any time. Files in use are removed on the next start.
options.radiante.download.tooltip: Downloaded on request from NVIDIA or Intel. Click to download or delete.
options.radiante.download.leave_world: Leave the world first: installing or deleting an upscaler needs a restart.
screen.radiante.download.restart.message: The change is ready. Restart the game now, as upscalers load at startup.
options.radiante.ray_tracing.tooltip: Switches between Radiante's ray traced renderer and Minecraft's own, like the Toggle Ray Tracing key (set it in Controls).
options.radiante.chunk_building_auto.too: Automatic sizes chunk building to your CPU (%s threads: %s chunk threads, batches of %s, %s at once). Manual shows the sliders.
message.radiante.showcase.singleplayer: Radiante: the showcase can only be built in a singleplayer world.
message.radiante.showcase.built: Radiante: showcase built to the east. Each room has a sign saying what to check. /radiante showcase 1-14 jumps to a room.
message.radiante.showcase.none: Radiante: no showcase built in this session. Stand where it should start and run /radiante showcase.
message.radiante.showcase.blocks: Radiante: every block laid out to the east, one category per group of rows, each with a sign.
message.radiante.biome.at: Radiante: %s (%s/%s) at %s %s %s. /radiante biome for the next one, /radiante biome back for the previous.
message.radiante.biome.not_found: Radiante: %s (%s/%s) not found within 6400 blocks. /radiante biome skips to the next.
message.radiante.biome.unknown: Radiante: no biome called %s in this dimension. /radiante biome list shows them.
How quickly exposure follows when you go from dark to light or back. Lower lets you see your eyes adjust; 100% is almost instant.
options.radiante.tunable.dof_strength.to: How strongly what is out of focus blurs. Needs Depth of Field.
options.radiante.tunable.dof_range.toolt: How much around what you look at stays sharp. Lower blurs sooner. Needs Depth of Field.
options.radiante.dof_auto_focus.tooltip: Focuses on the centre of the screen. Off keeps focus at Focus Distance, for screenshots. Changing it rebuilds the shaders.
options.radiante.tunable.dof_focus_dista: How far away the image is sharp when Auto Focus is off.
options.radiante.tunable.motion_blur_str: How long the smear of Motion Blur is.
options.radiante.tunable.fsr_sharpness.t: How much FSR sharpens the upscaled image. Higher is crisper but can show halos on edges.
options.radiante.tunable.low_light_boost: How much exposure may brighten a dark scene. Higher shows more in caves and at night; lower keeps the dark dark.
options.radiante.tunable.exposure_day.to: How bright the picture is kept by day. Lower is darker.
How bright the picture is kept at night. Lower is darker.
options.radiante.tunable.day_low_light_l: How far exposure may open by day in a dark place. Low keeps closed rooms dark; high brightens rooms lit only through a window.
options.radiante.tunable.mirror_smoothne: Metals at least this smooth are drawn as clean, sharp mirrors. 0% turns this off.
How much of the sky volumetric clouds cover.
options.radiante.tunable.cloud_quality.t: Steps per ray through volumetric clouds. Higher is smoother and slower.
options.radiante.tunable.fog_distance.to: How far volumetric fog and light shafts reach, in blocks.
options.radiante.star_altitude.tooltip: Stars get clearer the higher you are; at 100% they are twice as bright from a mountain top as from sea level. 0% keeps them the same everywhere.
options.radiante.tunable.stars.tooltip: How many stars the night sky has.
options.radiante.render_scale.tooltip: Share of the screen resolution traced before the upscaler scales it up. Lower is faster and softer. Custom mode only. Below 33% expect a very blurry, flickering image.
screen.radiante.download.dlss.switch: DLSS is installed. Switch to the DLSS pipeline now? It is recommended for your NVIDIA GPU. You can change it later in the settings.
screen.radiante.download.xess.switch: XeSS is installed. Switch to the XeSS pipeline now? You can change it later in the settings.
options.radiante.render_scale.limited.to: Share of the screen resolution traced before the upscaler scales it up. Lower is faster and softer; 50% to 67% is recommended. Custom mode only.
options.radiante.output_resolution.toolt:
Size the world is rendered at before a final FSR 1 upscale fills the window. HUD and text stay sharp.
Native: the window's own size.
1440p to 720p: a fixed height, saving the most on a 4K screen.
Custom: set it with Output Scale.
options.radiante.output_scale.tooltip: Share of the window's size the world is rendered at with Custom output resolution. Lower is faster and softer; HUD and text stay sharp.
Extra reflections inside reflections on top of Light Bounces, such as facing mirrors or water in a mirror. Needs a PBR pack for mirrors; water and glass always count.
options.radiante.share.tooltip: Your saved looks: keep the current one, switch between them, import a code someone sent you or copy one to share.
screen.radiante.share.title: Presets
screen.radiante.share.message: A look: lighting, sky, fog, water, tone and camera effects. Upscaler, frame generation and HDR are not included.
screen.radiante.share.copied: Code copied. Paste it wherever you want to share it.
screen.radiante.share.invalid: The clipboard does not hold a Radiante code.
screen.radiante.share.skipped: Imported. %s settings in the code are not known to this version and are skipped.
options.radiante.advanced.more: %s more in Advanced (turn it on below)
options.radiante.mod_overlays.tooltip: Lets other mods draw into the traced world, such as Litematica schematics, MiniHUD shapes and waypoint beams. Turn it off if a mod draws something wrong.
options.radiante.text_backgrounds.toolti: Draws the translucent plate behind text displays (leaderboards, holograms, server signs). Off shows only the letters.
screen.radiante.share.empty: No presets yet. Save your current look, or import a code from the clipboard.
screen.radiante.share.name: Name
screen.radiante.share.imported: Imported as %s. Pick Apply to use it.
screen.radiante.share.need_name: Type the new name in the box first.
screen.radiante.share.full: The preset could not be kept.
screen.radiante.share.name.hint: Name for the preset you save, import or rename...
screen.radiante.share.save.tooltip: Adds the look the game has now to the list, under the name typed above.
screen.radiante.share.paste.tooltip: Adds a preset from a shared code. Copy the code first; it is not applied until you pick Apply.
screen.radiante.share.apply.tooltip: Switches to the picked preset. Shaders are recompiled if the preset needs it. Clicking a preset twice does the same.
screen.radiante.share.copy.tooltip: Copies the picked preset as a code, to send to someone.
screen.radiante.share.rename.tooltip: Gives the picked preset the name typed above.
screen.radiante.share.delete.tooltip: Removes the picked preset from the list. Your current look is not changed.
screen.radiante.share.hint.in_use: This is the look the game has now.
screen.radiante.share.hint.apply: Pick Apply, or click it again, to switch to it.
screen.radiante.share.hint.pick: Pick a preset to see it here.
options.radiante.blocked.needs: No effect right now: turn on %s first.
options.radiante.blocked.needs_value: No effect right now: needs %s set to %s.
options.radiante.blocked.overridden: No effect right now: %s takes its place.
options.radiante.blocked.profile: Set by the renderer profile. Change it to turn the profile into Custom.
options.radiante.blocked.ray_tracing: No effect while Ray Tracing is off.
options.radiante.preset.tooltip: The denoiser and upscaler that finish the picture: DLSS Ray Reconstruction on NVIDIA RTX, or NRD with FSR or XeSS on any GPU. DLSS and XeSS download on first use.
options.radiante.debug_logging.tooltip: Writes extra renderer details to the game log for bug reports. Does not change the picture.
render_pipeline.module.ray_tracing.attri: Which glass Seamless Glass joins: blocks and panes, only blocks, or only panes.
options.radiante.notice.profile: Set by the %1$s profile. Changing it turns the profile into Custom; pick %1$s again to restore it.
options.radiante.notice.custom_profile: Custom: a profile's values with some settings changed by hand. Pick a profile again to restore its values.
options.radiante.blocked.bedrock_fog: No effect right now: Bedrock's fog does not use it. Works with Bedrock Volumetric Fog off under Advanced.

How resource pack normal and height maps are read. Nearest keeps the crisp pixel look; Bilinear smooths between pixels.
Volumetric clouds also show in reflections and through glass and water. Off is a little faster.
Steps through clouds seen in reflections and through glass. Higher is smoother and slower.
Steps towards the sun that shade clouds seen in reflections. Higher is more accurate and slower.
Steps for sky light on clouds seen in reflections. Higher is more accurate and slower.
Surfaces rougher than this stop reflecting volumetric clouds. Higher shows clouds on more surfaces, at a cost.
Height of the base of the volumetric cloud layer, in blocks. Raise it for higher clouds.
Height of the top of the volumetric cloud layer, in blocks. Further above the base gives taller, thicker clouds.
Scale of the large cloud shapes. Higher gives smaller, more frequent clouds; lower gives big, broad ones.
Scale of the fine detail that frays cloud edges. Higher gives finer, smaller wisps.
How cloudy the sky is in clear weather.
Steps towards the sun inside clouds, for their shading and the shadows they cast. Higher is more accurate and slower.
How soft the edges of cloud shadows on the ground are. Higher is softer.
Steps for sky light inside clouds. Higher gives smoother shaded sides and is slower.
How much sky light brightens clouds. Lower gives darker, moodier undersides.
Darkens thin cloud edges seen away from the sun, for a fluffier look. 0 turns it off.
Size of the patches of cloudy and clear sky. Higher gives smaller, more frequent patches.

The shape of the water surface.
Vanilla: the resource pack's own surface.
Realistic: fine, moving waves.
Bedrock: Bedrock's water pattern, needs its files.
Uses Bedrock RTX's own fog, a 50-block volume from the pack's fog settings, in place of biome haze and Radiante's fog.
How much Bedrock fog glows towards the sun. Higher gives a brighter halo around the sun and dimmer fog elsewhere.
How much light the air scatters in volumetric fog. Higher gives brighter light shafts and hazier air.
Brightness of the Bedrock sky, with Atmosphere set to Bedrock. Higher gives a brighter sky and more sky light.
How much sun and moon light the biome haze catches. Higher makes the haze glow more in sunlight.
How much light water scatters back. Higher gives brighter, milkier water; lower is darker and clearer.
Depth, in blocks, over which sunlight under water fades at the full rate. Deeper down it fades half as fast.
Brightness of the light filling the water around you while under water. Lower gives darker, deeper-looking water.
How murky water looks from above its surface. Lower lets you see deeper into it.
Decodes texture colours with the exact sRGB curve, as Bedrock RTX does. Dark colours come out slightly lighter.
Glass and water reflect by Bedrock RTX's formula, which changes how strongly they reflect at each angle.
Sunlight through glass and other see-through blocks takes their colour as in Bedrock RTX. Nearly opaque parts cast shadow.
The view through stained glass is tinted the way Bedrock RTX does it.
Glowing parts of Bedrock packs shine as brightly as in Bedrock RTX, following the pack's MER maps.
Sunlit surfaces under water show Bedrock RTX's moving caustic pattern.
Water dims light over at most 50 blocks, as in Bedrock RTX, so long views through water do not go black.
How wide the halo around the sun spreads. Higher gives a broader, softer glow.
How much the biome haze glows when you look towards the sun. Higher gives a brighter glow there and less elsewhere.
Caps how bright one spot of volumetric fog can get. Lower removes sparkles; higher allows brighter light shafts.

How water and glass share out reflection and refraction.
Deterministic: both traced every frame, sharper.
Stochastic: one picked at random per frame, cheaper but noisier.
How bright light-emitting blocks look when you see them directly. Does not change the light they cast.
How much light glowing blocks and held lights cast on their surroundings. Higher lights up rooms and caves more.
A faint base light on every surface, so unlit places are not pitch black. No effect under the renderer profiles.
Radius of the planet in the sky model, in km. Changes how the horizon and sunsets are coloured.
Radius of the outer edge of the atmosphere, in km. Further above the planet gives a thicker, hazier atmosphere.
How high the air that turns the sky blue reaches, in km. Higher gives a deeper blue sky and redder sunsets.
How high the haze near the ground reaches, in km. Higher gives a whiter, hazier sky.
How much the haze glows around the sun. Higher gives a tighter, brighter glow.
Lowest view angle the sky is worked out for. Below it the sky keeps the horizon's colour; higher raises that line.
Samples along each Motion Blur smear. Higher is smoother and slower.
Shifts the view by a fraction of a pixel each frame, so the upscaler and denoiser recover fine detail. Off is more jagged.
Caches bounced light in the world, so extra bounces are cheap and less noisy. Off is slower, and bounced light looks darker.
Shows the light cache's internal views instead of the picture. For debugging; keep it off.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.ant: How big a brightness change must be before the denoiser drops old frames. Lower reacts faster to light changes but flickers more.
How strongly the denoiser drops old frames when lighting changes. Higher leaves less ghosting but more noise.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.res: Surfaces smoother than this blend fewer frames, so their reflections keep up with motion. 0 turns it off.
Fewest frames those smooth surfaces still blend. Lower reacts faster but is noisier.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.max: Most frames the denoiser blends together. More is smoother but ghosts more on motion.
Frames in the denoiser's quick history, which catches sudden changes. Lower reacts faster but is noisier.
Frames used to steady the final picture. More is calmer; fewer reacts faster.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.his: For how many frames newly revealed areas get extra blur to hide their noise.
How far, in pixels, the extra blur on newly revealed areas reaches. Wider hides more noise but blurs more.
The same reach, in pixels, for the denoiser's alternate pass over newly revealed areas.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.fas: How tightly old frames are held to the quick history. Lower cuts ghosting but adds flicker.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.dif: Blur, in pixels, applied to bounced light before denoising. Higher removes more noise and fireflies but softens detail.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.spe: Blur, in pixels, applied to reflections before denoising. Higher removes more noise but softens reflections.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.min: How much nearby surfaces narrow the blur. Higher keeps contact shadows and corners sharper but can leave noise.
Smallest blur, in pixels, the denoiser uses. Higher is smoother but softer.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.max: Largest blur, in pixels, the denoiser uses on noisy areas. Higher cleans up more noise but smears detail.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.lob: How different reflection directions may be and still blend. Higher gives smoother but blurrier reflections.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.rou: How different surface roughness may be and still blend. Higher is smoother but mixes shiny and matte surfaces.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.pla: How far off a surface a neighbouring pixel may be and still blend. Lower keeps edges between surfaces sharper.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.spe: Reflection strength from which reflections start to follow the reflected object's motion. Lower reduces smearing in mirrors.
Reflection strength at which reflections fully follow the reflected object's motion.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.fir: How much brighter than its neighbours a pixel must be to count as a firefly. Lower removes more but can dim small highlights.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.min: Materials with a lower ID skip the bounced light denoiser. Leave it as it is unless debugging.
Materials with a lower ID skip the reflection denoiser. Leave it as it is unless debugging.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.che: Which half of the pixels holds the light when only half are traced. Off: every pixel is traced.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.ena: Removes isolated, very bright pixels (fireflies) from the denoised light.
render_pipeline.module.nrd.attribute.hit: Fills in missing hit distances from the neighbouring 3x3 or 5x5 pixels. Helps the denoiser where pixels traced no ray.
render_pipeline.module.post_render.attri: Size of the smallest stars. Each star gets a size between this and Star Max Size.
Size of the largest stars. Each star gets a size between Star Min Size and this.
How far away the star dome is drawn. Farther makes every star look smaller.
render_pipeline.module.tone_mapping.attr: Brightness auto exposure aims the average scene at. Higher is brighter overall.
Darkest light level, in stops, auto exposure measures. Anything darker is ignored.
Brightest light level, in stops, auto exposure measures. Anything brighter is ignored.
Share of the darkest pixels auto exposure leaves out, so a few black spots do not brighten the picture.
Pixels above this share are left out of auto exposure as highlights, so the sun and lamps do not darken the picture.
Lowest exposure auto exposure may use. Raise it to keep very bright scenes from going too dark.
Adjusts brightness to the scene, like an eye. Off uses Manual Exposure.

How auto exposure measures the scene.
Global: the whole picture.
Center: the middle of the screen.
The others: the light falling on the scene, as Bedrock does.
Size of the screen area Center metering looks at, in %.
Fixed exposure used when auto exposure is off. Higher is brighter.
Light level the White Point tone curves show as pure white. Higher keeps more highlight detail but looks darker.
Clips the final colours to the screen's range. Leave it on.
Bright light bleeds into a soft glow around it.
How strong bloom is. Higher gives a stronger glow around bright light.
How far bloom spreads. Higher gives a wider, softer glow.
Brightness below which nothing blooms. 0 lets everything glow a little.
Strength of the tightest bloom, right around bright spots.
Strength of the second, slightly wider bloom level.
Strength of the third, wider bloom level.
Strength of the widest bloom, the haze far around bright light.
Contrast around middle grey. Above 1 deepens darks and brightens lights.
Deepens (positive) or lifts (negative) the shadows darker than Shadow Contrast End.
Brightness below which Shadow Contrast acts. Higher reaches into brighter tones.
Gamma applied at the end. Changes how bright the mid-tones look.
Range of brightness, in stops, the Bedrock-style curve fits on screen. Higher keeps more shadow detail with less contrast.
Moves the Bedrock-style curve brighter or darker, in stops.
Most the Bedrock-style curve may brighten dark parts, in stops. 0 never lifts them.
Least contrast the Bedrock-style curve keeps in shadows. Higher keeps dark areas from going flat.
Bedrock's filmic saturation correction, which adjusts colour in bright parts like film. 0 turns it off.
Multiplies the red in the image. Above 1 is warmer.
Multiplies the green in the image.
Multiplies the blue in the image. Above 1 is cooler.
render_pipeline.module.xess_sr.attribute: Brightness hint passed to XeSS. Leave it at 1 unless XeSS ghosts or flickers in very bright or dark scenes.
options.radiante.blocked.bedrock_files: Bedrock not available: no Bedrock install (Minecraft for Windows) was found, and there are no Bedrock files in radiante/bedrock. Java is used instead.
options.radiante.cloud_height.tooltip: Raises or lowers the Vanilla clouds, in blocks above their usual height.
options.radiante.rebuild_shaders.tooltip: Applies the changes and builds the shaders again. Use it if the picture looks wrong after changing settings.
